title: Congruence from Transformation Sequences Core Test
description: Use rigid transformation sequences to prove congruence, identify corresponding parts, and reject non-rigid evidence.

questions.questionText: Which sequence is made only of rigid transformations?
options: Translate right 3, then rotate 90 degrees
Dilate by 2, then translate right 3
Stretch horizontally, then reflect
Enlarge the figure, then rotate
questions.correctAnswer: Translate right 3, then rotate 90 degrees
questions.explanation: Translations and rotations are both rigid, so their sequence preserves congruence.

questions.questionText: Triangle ABC is reflected across the x-axis to make triangle DEF. What must be true?
options: Triangle DEF is twice as large.
Only the areas are preserved.
Triangle ABC is congruent to triangle DEF.
Corresponding angles are cut in half.
questions.correctAnswer: Triangle ABC is congruent to triangle DEF.
questions.explanation: A reflection is rigid, so it preserves size and shape.

questions.questionText: A figure is translated 5 units left and then translated 2 units up. What conclusion is valid?
options: The final figure is similar but not congruent.
The final figure is congruent to the original.
The final figure has doubled side lengths.
The final figure has changed angle measures.
questions.correctAnswer: The final figure is congruent to the original.
questions.explanation: A sequence of translations is rigid.

questions.questionText: Which move would break a congruence proof?
options: Reflecting across the y-axis
Rotating 180 degrees
Translating down 4 units
Dilating by a scale factor of 3
questions.correctAnswer: Dilating by a scale factor of 3
questions.explanation: A dilation with scale factor other than 1 changes size.

questions.questionText: Quadrilateral PQRS maps to quadrilateral WXYZ by a rotation. Which pair of sides corresponds if P maps to W and Q maps to X?
options: PQ and WX
PQ and XY
PS and YZ
QR and WZ
questions.correctAnswer: PQ and WX
questions.explanation: Corresponding vertices follow the mapping order.

questions.questionText: A triangle is rotated and then reflected. What is preserved?
options: Only horizontal lengths
Only the location
Only the vertex names
All side lengths and angle measures
questions.correctAnswer: All side lengths and angle measures
questions.explanation: Rotations and reflections are rigid transformations.

questions.questionText: Which sentence best proves congruence?
options: The figures are both drawn on grid paper.
A sequence of rigid transformations maps one figure onto the other.
The figures have the same color.
The figures are in the same quadrant.
questions.correctAnswer: A sequence of rigid transformations maps one figure onto the other.
questions.explanation: A rigid mapping is strong evidence for congruence.

questions.questionText: A sequence includes a reflection, a translation, and a rotation. What kind of sequence is it?
options: A scaling sequence
A sequence that changes size
A rigid transformation sequence
A non-congruence sequence
questions.correctAnswer: A rigid transformation sequence
questions.explanation: Each listed move is rigid.

questions.questionText: If triangle ABC maps to triangle JKL by rigid transformations, which angle matches angle B?
options: angle K
angle J
angle L
angle C
questions.correctAnswer: angle K
questions.explanation: The second vertex B corresponds to the second vertex K.

questions.questionText: What is the main reason rigid transformations prove congruence?
options: They always keep coordinates positive.
They always keep orientation the same.
They preserve distance and angle measure.
They change every side length by the same factor.
questions.correctAnswer: They preserve distance and angle measure.
questions.explanation: Congruence depends on preserved size and shape.

questions.questionText: Triangle ABC is translated by <2, -5> and then reflected across the y-axis to make triangle A'B'C'. Which statement must be true?
options: AB is twice A'B'
angle A is half of angle A'
The triangles cannot be congruent after a reflection.
AB = A'B'
questions.correctAnswer: AB = A'B'
questions.explanation: Both transformations are rigid, so corresponding side lengths match.

questions.questionText: A student claims two figures are congruent because one can be rotated 180 degrees and then shifted onto the other. Is the claim justified?
options: No, because a translation changes side lengths.
Yes, because both moves are rigid transformations.
No, because a 180 degree rotation changes angle measures.
Yes, but only if both figures are in Quadrant I.
questions.correctAnswer: Yes, because both moves are rigid transformations.
questions.explanation: Rotation and translation preserve distance and angle measure.

questions.questionText: A rectangle is reflected across the y-axis, then dilated by 1/2. Is the final rectangle congruent to the original?
options: No, because the dilation changes side lengths.
Yes, because the reflection is rigid.
Yes, because the final figure is still a rectangle.
No, because reflections change angle measures.
questions.correctAnswer: No, because the dilation changes side lengths.
questions.explanation: One non-rigid step is enough to break congruence.

questions.questionText: Triangle MNO maps to triangle RST. If M maps to R, N maps to S, and O maps to T, which congruence statement is correctly ordered?
options: triangle MNO congruent to triangle RTS
triangle MON congruent to triangle RST
triangle MNO congruent to triangle RST
triangle NMO congruent to triangle RST
questions.correctAnswer: triangle MNO congruent to triangle RST
questions.explanation: Congruence statements must list corresponding vertices in matching order.

questions.questionText: Figure A is reflected across a vertical line and then translated. Which property may change?
options: Side lengths
Orientation
Angle measures
Congruence to the original
questions.correctAnswer: Orientation
questions.explanation: A reflection can reverse orientation, but rigid moves keep size and shape.

questions.questionText: A polygon has side lengths 4, 5, 7, and 9. Its image after a transformation sequence has side lengths 4, 5, 7, and 9. What extra evidence best supports congruence?
options: The image has different vertex names.
The image is farther from the origin.
The image is drawn with a darker line.
The image was made by translations, rotations, and reflections.
questions.correctAnswer: The image was made by translations, rotations, and reflections.
questions.explanation: A rigid transformation sequence proves all corresponding parts are preserved.

questions.questionText: Point A maps to D, point B maps to E, and point C maps to F after a rigid sequence. Which side corresponds to BC?
options: EF
DE
DF
AB
questions.correctAnswer: EF
questions.explanation: Match the endpoints: B maps to E and C maps to F.

questions.questionText: A figure is translated, reflected, then stretched vertically. Which conclusion is correct?
options: The sequence is rigid because it starts with a translation.
The final figure must be congruent.
The reflection cancels the stretch.
The sequence does not guarantee congruence.
questions.correctAnswer: The sequence does not guarantee congruence.
questions.explanation: A stretch changes distances, so the full sequence is not rigid.

questions.questionText: Two triangles are congruent because triangle ABC can be mapped exactly onto triangle XYZ by a rigid sequence. If angle C is 48 degrees, what is the corresponding angle measure?
options: 42 degrees
96 degrees
48 degrees
It cannot be known because the triangle moved.
questions.correctAnswer: 48 degrees
questions.explanation: Rigid transformations preserve angle measure.

questions.questionText: Which observation is not enough by itself to prove two figures are congruent?
options: A translation maps one exactly onto the other.
Both figures have area 36 square units.
A rotation maps one exactly onto the other.
A reflection followed by a translation maps one exactly onto the other.
questions.correctAnswer: Both figures have area 36 square units.
questions.explanation: Equal area alone does not guarantee matching side lengths and angles.

questions.questionText: A student writes: triangle ABC congruent to triangle DEF. Which detail must be checked?
options: A matches D, B matches E, and C matches F.
A and D have the same x-coordinate.
Both triangles are above the x-axis.
The letters are alphabetically ordered.
questions.correctAnswer: A matches D, B matches E, and C matches F.
questions.explanation: The order of vertices communicates corresponding parts.

questions.questionText: A trapezoid is rotated 90 degrees clockwise and then translated left. Which statement is always true?
options: The trapezoid becomes similar but larger.
The trapezoid's angles all increase by 90 degrees.
The trapezoid remains congruent to its original image.
The trapezoid must stay in the same quadrant.
questions.correctAnswer: The trapezoid remains congruent to its original image.
questions.explanation: A rotation followed by a translation is a rigid sequence.

questions.questionText: Which sequence could prove triangle ABC is congruent to triangle A'B'C'?
options: Dilate by 2, then rotate 90 degrees
Stretch horizontally, then translate up
Compress vertically, then reflect
Reflect across the x-axis, then translate right 6
questions.correctAnswer: Reflect across the x-axis, then translate right 6
questions.explanation: Only the first sequence uses rigid transformations throughout.

questions.questionText: A rigid sequence maps segment AB onto segment CD. If AB = 11 units, what is CD?
options: 5.5 units
11 units
22 units
Cannot be determined after movement
questions.correctAnswer: 11 units
questions.explanation: Rigid transformations preserve distance.

questions.questionText: Why can a reflected figure still be congruent to the original?
options: A reflection changes orientation but preserves side lengths and angles.
A reflection doubles every side length.
A reflection keeps every coordinate unchanged.
A reflection changes angle measures but not area.
questions.correctAnswer: A reflection changes orientation but preserves side lengths and angles.
questions.explanation: Congruence allows changed orientation.

questions.questionText: A sequence maps quadrilateral ABCD to quadrilateral EFGH. Which angle corresponds to angle D?
options: angle E
angle F
angle G
angle H
questions.correctAnswer: angle H
questions.explanation: The fourth vertex D maps to the fourth vertex H.

questions.questionText: A triangle is moved by two transformations. The first is a rotation and the second is unknown. Which second move keeps the final image congruent?
options: Dilate by 4
Reflect across the y-axis
Stretch vertically
Scale by 1/3
questions.correctAnswer: Reflect across the y-axis
questions.explanation: A reflection is rigid; the other choices change size.

questions.questionText: A figure and its image have matching side lengths and angles. Which statement would be the strongest explanation?
options: The image is close to the original.
The image has the same number of vertices.
A rigid sequence maps the figure exactly onto its image.
The image is drawn on a square grid.
questions.correctAnswer: A rigid sequence maps the figure exactly onto its image.
questions.explanation: The mapping explains why corresponding measurements match.

questions.questionText: Triangle ABC is reflected and translated to triangle PQR. If AB corresponds to PQ and BC corresponds to QR, which side corresponds to AC?
options: PR
PQ
QR
AB
questions.correctAnswer: PR
questions.explanation: A and C map to P and R, so AC maps to PR.

questions.questionText: A sequence of transformations maps one figure onto another, but one side changes from 8 units to 12 units. What can you conclude?
options: The figures are definitely congruent.
Only the labels changed.
The sequence was not entirely rigid.
The side change proves a reflection occurred.
questions.correctAnswer: The sequence was not entirely rigid.
questions.explanation: Rigid transformations cannot change side length.

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly compares congruent and similar figures?
options: Congruent figures may be scaled by any factor.
Similar figures always have matching side lengths.
Congruent figures only need equal area.
Congruent figures need the same size and shape; similar figures may be scaled.
questions.correctAnswer: Congruent figures need the same size and shape; similar figures may be scaled.
questions.explanation: Congruence does not allow a size change.

questions.questionText: If triangle ABC is congruent to triangle LMN, which side corresponds to LN?
options: AB
AC
BC
MN
questions.correctAnswer: AC
questions.explanation: The first and third vertices correspond: A to L and C to N.

questions.questionText: A sequence includes only rotations around the origin and translations. What is preserved after the whole sequence?
options: Perimeter and angle measures
Perimeter only, not angles
Angles only, not side lengths
Neither perimeter nor angles
questions.correctAnswer: Perimeter and angle measures
questions.explanation: Rotations and translations are rigid, so both lengths and angles are preserved.

questions.questionText: A student says every sequence of transformations proves congruence. What is the correction?
options: Every transformation preserves size.
Dilations always preserve congruence.
Stretching proves congruence better than reflection.
Only sequences made entirely of rigid transformations prove congruence.
questions.correctAnswer: Only sequences made entirely of rigid transformations prove congruence.
questions.explanation: Some transformations change size or shape.

questions.questionText: A figure is reflected over the x-axis. Which later transformation would still keep the final image congruent?
options: Dilate by 5
Stretch horizontally
Rotate 90 degrees
Compress vertically
questions.correctAnswer: Rotate 90 degrees
questions.explanation: A rotation is rigid and preserves congruence.

questions.questionText: Triangle ABC has vertices A(1, 2), B(4, 2), C(1, 6). Triangle DEF is the image after a translation and reflection. Which evidence is strongest for congruence?
options: Both triangles have vertices with integer coordinates.
A rigid sequence maps A to D, B to E, and C to F.
Both triangles are on the same coordinate plane.
Both triangles use three-letter names.
questions.correctAnswer: A rigid sequence maps A to D, B to E, and C to F.
questions.explanation: A rigid mapping with corresponding vertices proves congruence.

questions.questionText: A sequence maps quadrilateral ABCD onto EFGH. AB = 6, BC = 9, angle C = 110 degrees. Which must be true?
options: EF = 6, FG = 9, and angle G = 110 degrees.
EH = 6, FG = 18, and angle G = 55 degrees.
EF = 12, FG = 9, and angle C = 110 degrees.
AB = 6, BC = 9, and angle E = 110 degrees.
questions.correctAnswer: EF = 6, FG = 9, and angle G = 110 degrees.
questions.explanation: Corresponding parts follow the mapping order ABCD to EFGH.

questions.questionText: A triangle is translated, rotated, reflected, and then dilated by scale factor 1. Which conclusion is valid?
options: The final triangle is not congruent because every dilation changes size.
The final triangle has doubled side lengths.
The final triangle is congruent to the original.
The final triangle is congruent only if it stayed in the same quadrant.
questions.correctAnswer: The final triangle is congruent to the original.
questions.explanation: A dilation by scale factor 1 does not change size.

questions.questionText: A figure is transformed by a sequence and the final image has all angles preserved but every side length doubled. What best describes the relationship?
options: The figures are congruent.
The figures are unrelated because angles stayed the same.
The figures are congruent if the area also doubled.
The figures are similar but not congruent.
questions.correctAnswer: The figures are similar but not congruent.
questions.explanation: Congruence requires matching side lengths, not just matching angles.

questions.questionText: Triangle ABC is congruent to triangle RQP. Which correspondence is correct?
options: A corresponds to Q.
B corresponds to Q.
C corresponds to R.
AB corresponds to RP.
questions.correctAnswer: B corresponds to Q.
questions.explanation: The ordered statement pairs A with R, B with Q, and C with P.

questions.questionText: A student proves congruence by saying: 'Both shapes have perimeter 30.' What is the flaw?
options: Equal perimeter does not guarantee matching side lengths and angles.
Congruent figures can never have equal perimeter.
Perimeter changes under every translation.
Only area matters for congruence.
questions.correctAnswer: Equal perimeter does not guarantee matching side lengths and angles.
questions.explanation: Perimeter alone is too weak; different shapes can share a perimeter.

questions.questionText: A reflection maps triangle ABC to triangle A'B'C'. Then a translation maps A'B'C' to triangle XYZ. Which statement is justified?
options: triangle ABC is similar but not congruent to triangle XYZ
triangle ABC has half the area of triangle XYZ
triangle XYZ must face the same direction as triangle ABC
triangle ABC is congruent to triangle XYZ
questions.correctAnswer: triangle ABC is congruent to triangle XYZ
questions.explanation: The whole sequence is rigid, so the first and final triangles are congruent.

questions.questionText: A rigid sequence maps point A to point D, B to E, and C to F. Which conclusion would be invalid?
options: AB equals DE.
angle B equals angle E.
The area must change because the coordinates changed.
triangle ABC is congruent to triangle DEF.
questions.correctAnswer: The area must change because the coordinates changed.
questions.explanation: Changing coordinates does not imply changing size.

questions.questionText: Which sequence cannot be used to prove congruence?
options: Reflect, translate, then rotate
Rotate, translate, then dilate by 2
Translate, rotate, then reflect
Rotate 180 degrees, reflect, then translate
questions.correctAnswer: Rotate, translate, then dilate by 2
questions.explanation: The dilation by 2 changes size.

questions.questionText: Triangle ABC is congruent to triangle DEF. If DE = 14 and EF = 9, which original sides match those lengths?
options: AB = 14 and BC = 9
AC = 14 and AB = 9
BC = 14 and AC = 9
DF = 14 and DE = 9
questions.correctAnswer: AB = 14 and BC = 9
questions.explanation: A maps to D, B maps to E, and C maps to F.

questions.questionText: A figure is rotated 90 degrees clockwise and then reflected across the y-axis. What can you say about orientation and congruence?
options: Orientation and side lengths must both change.
Congruence is lost because a reflection is not rigid.
Orientation may change, but congruence is preserved.
The figure is congruent only if orientation stays the same.
questions.correctAnswer: Orientation may change, but congruence is preserved.
questions.explanation: Rigid transformations may change orientation without changing size or shape.

questions.questionText: Two figures are congruent. Which explanation is most precise?
options: They are both polygons.
They have the same approximate area.
They look alike when drawn small.
There exists a sequence of rigid transformations that maps one exactly onto the other.
questions.correctAnswer: There exists a sequence of rigid transformations that maps one exactly onto the other.
questions.explanation: Congruence is established by exact matching through rigid motion.

questions.questionText: A transformation sequence maps a square of side 5 to a square of side 5 in a new location. Is that alone a complete proof of congruence?
options: Yes, any two figures with one equal side are congruent.
No, but matching all sides and right angles or giving a rigid sequence would complete the proof.
No, squares can never be congruent after moving.
Yes, location alone proves congruence.
questions.correctAnswer: No, but matching all sides and right angles or giving a rigid sequence would complete the proof.
questions.explanation: The explanation should establish all corresponding measurements or a rigid mapping.

questions.questionText: A sequence maps pentagon ABCDE to pentagon VWXYZ. Which side corresponds to CD?
options: XY
VW
WX
YZ
questions.correctAnswer: XY
questions.explanation: C maps to X and D maps to Y, so CD maps to XY.

questions.questionText: A student sees a figure reflected and says it cannot be congruent because clockwise order became counterclockwise. What should you say?
options: The student is right because congruent figures must keep orientation.
Reflections can reverse orientation and still preserve congruence.
The image is congruent only if a dilation follows.
The reflection changes every angle measure.
questions.correctAnswer: Reflections can reverse orientation and still preserve congruence.
questions.explanation: Orientation can reverse while distances and angles stay the same.
